terms.meaning: the set of database tables that hold match moments

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and purpose
sections.what: Brings in the database types and client, the rights check and the incident input type. The file states that rights are checked before anything is stored.
sections.why: Likely reason: the store is the one place that saves match incidents.
sections.watch_out: The rights check is imported here, but the code using it is not in the visible part, so this cannot be confirmed.

sections.name: appendIncidents
sections.title: Saves new incidents for an event
sections.what: Stores a batch of incoming incident records for one event after checking each record's source is allowed to be stored. Records already stored are skipped, so re-running an import does not make copies, and the number of newly saved records is returned.
sections.why: The code comment says this is idempotent, so repeat imports are safe.
sections.watch_out: Duplicate protection relies on a uniqueness rule in the database; if that rule is missing, repeat imports create duplicate records.

sections.name: incidentsObservedBy
sections.title: Reads incidents as known at a time
sections.what: Returns an event's incidents recorded on or before a cutoff time, optionally limited to those that took effect by a second time, in match clock order. This lets a view show what was known at a given moment, without later corrections.
sections.why: Each incident has two times (when it happened and when it was recorded), so past views can be rebuilt exactly.
sections.watch_out: Results are sorted by the match clock first, then sequence, so changing the sort order changes every total built on top.

sections.name: eventExists
sections.title: Checks an event is stored
sections.what: Answers yes or no for whether an event with a given id is in the database. Replay uses it to return a clear No such event message.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its name; it is a cheap check before heavier loading.
sections.watch_out: It only checks that the event exists, not whether it is ready to show.
